newsitem.title: UK: Protean warns German unit woes to hit profit.
newsitem.headline: Protean warns German unit woes to hit profit.

text.p: Laboratory equipment supplier and water purification specialist Protean Plc said year profits would be "materially lower than current market expectations" following problems at its DWA unit in Germany.
It said the DWA water purification unit's contribution to interim results, due on September 30, was now expected to be around 1.25 million stg lower than original expectations.
The shares fell 83-1/2 pence to 166 pence by 0732 GMT.
Protean said there had been "a very recent serious deterioration in the financial performance" of its DWA unit.
It said Armin Bechtel had left as managing director of DWA and been replaced by Anita Sayer, formerly managing director of Elga Ltd.
Protean said it felt the "appropriate management initiatives are now being taken."
It said elsewhere in the group, trading conditions "whilst difficult are not significantly different from expectations."
It added that it intended to maintain the interim dividend.
Protean reported a 37 percent jump in full year pretax profits to 10.3 million stg from 7.5 million stg in June and paid out a total dividend of 6.6 pence, up from 5.4 pence.
